speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand your episodes of unresponsiveness, how long does each episode last, and are you aware of what is happening during them? Additionally, have you noticed any specific triggers like flashing lights or emotional stress?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the post-ictal confusion and specific aura suggest a seizure. To differentiate between focal and generalized onset, and to rule out other causes, I need to know if there is a family history of epilepsy or if these episodes are triggered by sleep deprivation or flashing lights. REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Impaired Awareness Seizure (likely Frontal Lobe Epilepsy)
